If you believe Einstein, we cannot travel faster than the speed of light. But it hardly matters as, even with our best technology, we have no way to even get to the speed of light. Typically travelling, at best, a significant fraction of the speed of light I did a quick google search and found that the fastest recorded speed of any man made object is the Parker solar probe, which hit an astonishing 394,736 miles per hour. Surely that must be pretty close to the speed of light, right? Well, actually, the speed of light is 186,000 miles/sec which works out to 669,600,000. MPH. And that is if you assume you can instantly hit that speed. Which you can’t. So lets say 7,000 years to get there. And you show up and the planet has NO usable resources and simply cannot sustain you. It would be like spending a year on the ocean only to show up on a barren rock that had no plant or animal life, No fish in the waters around it and, in this case, no oxygen. People simply do not understand the fantastically ridiculous challenges that would have to me overcome to get there and the fact that there is literally no reason to go. ***Edit 7/12/2024*** Note: I found a math error in my time estimate to Proxima Centauri that threw off my time estimate by around 7140 years.
